title: openai-bridge: v13 Responses compatibility - forward seed + structured attrs passthrough
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Forward OpenAI Responses v13 `seed`/determinism hints and structured-attributes (metadata) through the bridge; stabilize streaming framing for mixed text/tool chunks; add tests and docs note.
description:
Summary: Implement compatibility for the OpenAI Responses v13 semantics: propagate explicit seed/determinism hints and preserve per-token + per-segment structured attributes (metadata) end-to-end through Redwood's OpenAI bridge and streaming path. This PR focuses on three areas: 1) pass-through of the `seed`/`determinism` hint on both sync and streaming paths; 2) canonical mapping of Responses v13 structured attributes (attrs) into Redwood internal ResponseAttributes and back to downstream clients (OpenAI-compatible shape for function/tool call chunks); 3) streaming stability fixes for mixed chunks (text + tool call signals) to avoid reordering and partial-attribute drop during reassembly.

Motivation and context: Responses v13 introduces an expanded attributes envelope used by model tooling and evals teams to annotate segments with deterministic hints, provenance tags, and tooling handshake signals. Customers using Redwood's OpenAI-compat layer rely on exact propagation of these attributes for deterministic replay, offering strong guarantees for A/B and canary rollouts. Previously we preserved `seed` metadata in v11/12 adapters, but v13 adds nested structured attrs and a slight framing change for tool-call boundaries. Without correct passthrough, downstream SDKs and replay systems lose deterministic replay and function-handshake attributes, causing surprising behavior for customers using seed-based reruns or external tool orchestators.

What this PR changes (single-line checklist): - add request/response mapping for Responses v13 attributes -> Redwood ResponseAttributes -> OpenAI-compatible attribute passthrough; - wire `seed`/`determinism` on both REST and streaming code paths; - canonical mapping of Responses v13 structured attributes (attrs) into Redwood internal ResponseAttributes and back to downstream clients (OpenAI-compatible shape for function/tool call chunks); - streaming stability fixes for mixed chunks (text + tool call signals) to avoid reordering and partial-attribute drop during reassembly.

Implementation notes (high-level commits): commit 1: bridge: add v13 attribute serializer/deserializer and mapping table; commit 2: core/stream: change ReassemblyBuffer to attach attribute-frames and ensure monotonic attribute offsets; commit 3: api/compat: include seed header propagation for http/streaming requests and include fallback when absent; commit 4: tests: deterministic-replay integration test + new test vectors generated (golden files); commit 5: docs: add section "OpenAI Responses v13: seed & structured attrs passthrough".

Files changed (high-level): - src/compat/openai/v13_adapter.go (new mapping & serializer) - src/serving/stream/reassembly.go (stream/frame reassembly fixes) - src/serving/stream/stream_test.go (new integration vectors) - api/compat/http_adapter.go (seed passthrough on REST) - docs/openai/v13-compat.md (docs snippet) - testdata/responses-v13/* (golden chunk captures) - tools/generate_v13_vectors.py (helper used in tests) - go.mod / go.sum (minor deps)

Small illustrative snippet (v13 attr mapping):
 // v13 attr shape -> Redwood internal
 {"attrs": [{"k":"seed","v":12345},{"k":"provenance","v":"eval-run"}],"segment_type":"tool_call"}
 becomes
 ResponseAttributes{Seed:12345, Tags:["eval-run"], SegmentType:ToolCall}
 and when re-emitted to an OpenAI-compatible consumer we preserve the attrs envelope and add `redwood.bridge_id` tag.

Testing and QA: - unit tests for mapping both directions (v13 <-> internal) - integration test that opens a streaming connection, sends split tool-call chunks with interleaved attributes and asserts the reassembled final response keeps attribute boundaries and the seed value; uses recorded golden frames in testdata/responses-v13/ - smoke test with SDK: redwood-sdk-python example `examples/openai_v13_seed_demo.py` (added) - manual QA plan: exercise deterministic replay by re-sending request with seed and comparing token stream equality between two runs on same pinned model.

Backward compatibility: The adapter is additive: when v13 attrs are not present we default to current behavior. We preserve existing v11/v12 mappings via a compatibility shim. No customer-facing API changes except improved passthrough fidelity for v13 consumers.

Review notes and important tradeoffs: - We intentionally keep the mapping conservative: complex nested attr payloads are preserved as opaque kv lists instead of being normalized into typed fields beyond `seed` and `segment_type`. This avoids breaking future v13 evolution. - The streaming reassembly change attaches small attribute-metadata to chunk envelopes which increases envelope memory a small amount (benchmarked ~2% at 512-concurrency); we add an optimization flag to disable attribute retention if customers opt out for ultra-low memory environments.

Manual rollback plan: revert the v13 adapter and reassembly change together (single commit) and redeploy; the change is behind a feature flag in config (openai_v13_attrs_passthrough=true) to allow staged rollout.

Changelog entry (short): Add OpenAI Responses v13 seed and structured-attributes passthrough to the OpenAI compatibility bridge.

Merge outcome: merged via squash-and-merge to main. Merge commit message preserved summary and Linear links. Feature gated on config flag `openai_v13_attrs_passthrough` and enabled for canary region us-east-1 for first 48h.
